connector: Caspian has his army now: bears, Mice, Centaurs, Dwarfs and one Giant. Tonight they hold a council, and every group wants something different. Watch the arguing, then watch for the moment someone has to choose. A good leader listens first and decides second.

a.raw: because nikabrik distrusted doctor cornelius he reached for his sword although caspian called the doctor his greatest friend
a.fixed: Because Nikabrik distrusted Doctor Cornelius, he reached for his sword although Caspian called the Doctor his greatest friend.
a.why: Capitals start the sentence and name the characters; a comma after the opening because clause; no comma before although at the end; a period ends it.

b.raw: when the great night came caspians heart swelled because he saw how many had come
b.fixed: When the great night came, Caspian’s heart swelled because he saw how many had come.
b.why: Capital W starts it; a comma after the opening when clause; capital C and an apostrophe in Caspian’s; no comma before because at the end; a period ends it.

notes.wgrd: Find the conflict (who is set against whom, and what is at stake) and the moment of choice: who decides, and how.
vocab: A group gathered to talk and decide what to do.
The chief steward who runs a lord’s household.
Ditches and banks dug for defense.
Companions, especially of a king or queen.
notes.wordParts: Latin bases: spect = look, ject = throw, script and scribe = write: inspect, reject, manuscript, spectacles.
notes.grammar: A complex sentence has a main clause and a dependent clause that starts with a word like because, although, when, if or since. If the dependent clause comes first, put a comma after it.
notes.spelling: Schwa is the lazy uh sound in an unstressed syllable. Your ear can’t spell it, so find a related word where that vowel is stressed: definite from finite, composition from compose.

virtue.title: Which pillar is it?
virtue.intro: The OAO Seven Pillars are honesty, respect, courtesy, responsibility, courage, service and perseverance. In Chapter 7, Caspian’s army meets, fights and nearly loses. Read each moment. Tap the pillar it shows best.

items.t: Nikabrik calls Doctor Cornelius a half-and-halfer. Caspian says, “This is my greatest friend and the saviour of my life. And anyone who doesn’t like his company may leave my army: at once.”
items.why: Caspian stands up for his friend in front of everyone.
items.hint: Whose side does Caspian take, and in front of whom?

items.t: Trufflehunter says it is time to blow the Horn. Caspian answers, “We are certainly in great need. But it is hard to be sure we are at our greatest.”
items.why: He thinks hard before using the one treasure he was told to save.
items.hint: What was Caspian told about the Horn?

items.t: Trumpkin doesn’t believe in the Horn, but he says, “Send me, Sire, I’ll go.” He will travel through enemy country to Cair Paravel.
items.why: He takes on a dangerous job for his King.
items.hint: What is the job, and is it safe?

items.t: Trumpkin says, “I know the difference between giving advice and taking orders. You’ve had my advice, and now it’s the time for orders.”
items.why: He says what he thinks, then follows his King’s decision.
items.hint: What does Trumpkin do after he disagrees?

transcripts.welcome: Hello, it’s Nell. Caspian has an army now, a strange and wonderful one. Tonight it meets in council, and everybody has an idea. Today’s question: when everyone around a leader is arguing, what should the leader do?
transcripts.read: Listen to each group at the council. The Bears want supper first. The Mice want to charge. The Moles want to dig. Ask what each idea tells you about who they are. Then watch for the moment the arguing stops and someone decides.
transcripts.morphology: Three more Latin bases. Spect means look, so to respect someone is to look up to them. Ject means throw, so eject means throw out. Script and scribe mean write, and a scribe is a person whose job is writing. Find the base, and the word starts to explain itself.
